checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are accurate and rigorous. It correctly identified that the image fails the primary geometric definition of the class (cylindrical metal aerosol can) by showing rectangular plastic bottles instead. The Router was not too lenient; in fact, it correctly marked 'Cap is dome-shaped...' as present only in a loose sense, but the failure of the main container shape is the dominant alignment issue. The Router correctly marked functional components like the spray nozzle and specific label text as missing/false.
artifact_review: The Router's artifact detection is strong. It correctly flagged 'text_gibberish' (Severity 4) which is confirmed by the Image Text Auditor returning empty blocks. The 'structural_collapse' of the caps (Severity 3) is also well-observed; the Expert Topology Auditor found a high-confidence mask, but this only confirms the object exists as a blob, not that it has correct internal mechanical structure (which the Router noted is missing). The Router did not underestimate severities. The 'texture_anomaly' on the mesh is a valid minor artifact.
alignment_reasoning: The image fundamentally fails the taxonomy definition. The class 'hair spray' is defined as a cylindrical metal aerosol can. The image shows rectangular plastic pump/squeeze bottles. The Fine Grained Classifier supports this misalignment, ranking 'sunscreen' and 'lotion' higher than 'hair spray'. Only superficial features (vibrant colors, glossy surface) match. This is a severe semantic and structural mismatch, warranting a very low alignment score similar to the 'bannister' reference where the object class is wrong.
artifact_reasoning: Major artifacts include severe text gibberish (illegible labels) and structural simplification of mechanical parts (caps lack internal pumps/nozzles, appearing as melted plastic). While the overall lighting and color are good (Perceptual Quality Auditor found no noise/blur), the structural integrity of the product packaging is compromised. The severity is moderate-to-high due to the functional implausibility of the containers.
key_defects: Wrong container geometry (rectangular plastic vs cylindrical metal)
Structural collapse of cap mechanisms (missing internal parts)
